---
title: "Week 7 Exercises - Quarto, LaTeX Math, and AI Assistants"
---

Short, **ungraded** practice tasks - about 30 minutes. Companion reading: [Ch. 16](../book/chapters/16-quarto-documents.html), [Ch. 17](../book/chapters/17-latex-basics.html), and [Ch. 18](../book/chapters/18-ai-assisted-coding.html). These tasks build the skills your final project write-up needs - start that write-up as a `.qmd` this week.

1.  In Positron, create a new Quarto document (Command Palette → **Quarto: New Document**), give it a title and your name in the YAML header, and render it to HTML (`Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K`).
2.  Add an R code chunk that reads the stickleback data and prints `dim(stickle)`. Render again.
3.  Add a chunk that makes one ggplot figure, with a `label` and `fig-cap` chunk option, and render.
4.  Hide the code of the figure chunk with `echo: false` - the figure should remain.
5.  Add inline math (a mean, `$\bar{x}$`) and one display equation (e.g., the standard error) between `$$` fences.
6.  Add a callout block (`::: {.callout-note}`) with a note to your future self.
7.  Cross-reference your figure from the text with `@fig-...`.
8.  Restart R, clear everything, and render one more time: does the document run cleanly from scratch? (If not, something lives only in your console - fix that.)
9.  If you have TinyTeX installed, switch `format: html` to `format: pdf` and render. Read the error log if it fails - what is it asking for?
10. Take one error message you hit this week, paste it into an AI assistant, and ask for an explanation. Then *verify* the explanation against the documentation. Where was it right, incomplete, or wrong?
11. **Before next Monday (Talapas week)**: confirm your cluster account works - log in to Open OnDemand at <https://ondemand.talapas.uoregon.edu> with your Duck ID. If you cannot get in, contact me *now*, not next week.
